references.text: The first time Hagar fled into the wilderness, the angel of the Lord found her at a spring. This event is a strong parallel to Gen 21:19, where God again provides Hagar with water in the wilderness.
The Lord opened Balaam's eyes so that he saw the angel of the Lord—a direct parallel to God opening Hagar's eyes so that she saw the well.

Elisha asked that the Lord would open his servant's eyes, and he saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire. The same expression is used regarding Hagar—God opens eyes to see what is already there.
Just as God opened Hagar's eyes to see a well with water, Jesus opened the blind man's eyes, demonstrating God's power to give sight and provision.
Abraham lifted his gaze and saw a ram caught in the thicket—a parallel to Hagar seeing the well: God provides at the decisive moment.
